outputs.explanation: Main panel is a scatter plot where each of the 141 individual samples is plotted as its own marker; the marginal histograms show the full distribution of these individual samples/counts. Scatter plots and histograms are exempt from requiring additional overlay of individual points.

Caption states each point represents the mean ± s.d. of 6 samples per reporter (technical/biological replicates averaged per cell line). This is an averaged-data plot (not raw individual scatter), and no underlying individual replicate measurements are overlaid on the mean±SD markers.
These are smoothed density/line curves showing distributions of subtype-averaged periods and amplitudes. Line plots are exempt from requiring individual point overlay.
This is a box plot (explicitly exempt category) and individual sample values are additionally overlaid as dots on top of each box, per the caption and legend (Per2-Luc/Bmal1-Luc reporter dots).

Polar histograms display the probability distribution of phase differences over time built from the underlying individual measurements; as a histogram-type distribution plot it does not require a separate overlay of individual points.

Polar histogram showing the distribution of phase differences averaged by subtype; as with panel E, this is a histogram/distribution-type plot, which is exempt from requiring individual point overlay.

This is an illustrative line-plot example of a single signal trace with a fitted curve and decay envelope, not a summary/average plot across multiple samples. Line plots are exempt from the individual-points requirement.

Each of the 117 samples is plotted individually as its own point (scatter plot), with error bars reflecting fit parameter uncertainty for that single sample rather than variability across replicates. Scatter plots are exempt since the points themselves are the individual data.
